You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/mptcp/pm.c`

- Added `bh_lock_sock(sk)` at the beginning of the `mptcp_pm_add_timer()` function, before any socket state is accessed.
- Added a check `if (sock_owned_by_user(sk))`: if the socket is locked by user context, the timer is rescheduled (`sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + HZ / 20)`) and execution jumps to the `out` label to avoid touching the socket while it is in use.
- Added `bh_unlock_sock(sk)` in the `out` label to release the lock after all socket operations are done.

### Relationships

These modifications work together to fix a potential data-race condition in the MPTCP ADD_ADDR retransmission timer:
- The timer runs in softirq context, while the socket may be accessed concurrently from process context (e.g., via system calls).
- By acquiring the bottom-half socket lock (`bh_lock_sock`), concurrent access is prevented.
- The ownership check (`sock_owned_by_user`) ensures that if the socket is already locked by user context, the timer safely defers its work instead of spinning or corrupting state.
- The lock is released via `bh_unlock_sock` after the path manager operations are done, maintaining proper lock ordering and allowing other contexts to proceed.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (inet_sk_state_load(sk) == TCP_CLOSE) return;</text>
<text>if (mptcp_pm_should_add_signal_addr(msk)) { sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + TCP_RTO_MAX / 8); goto out; }</text>
<text></text>
Reason:
These statements access and modify socket/MPTCP state from `mptcp_pm_add_timer()` which runs in softirq context without holding `bh_lock_sock()`. This allows concurrent access from process context, leading to a data-race.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>bh_lock_sock(sk);</text>
<text>if (sock_owned_by_user(sk)) { sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + HZ / 20); goto out; }</text>
<text>bh_unlock_sock(sk);</text>
Reason:
`bh_lock_sock()` ensures the socket lock is held in softirq context, serializing access with process-context code. The `sock_owned_by_user()` check detects if user context holds the lock; if so, the timer is rescheduled to avoid blocking, and execution jumps to `out:` where `bh_unlock_sock()` releases the lock. This prevents data corruption while allowing the retry logic to proceed safely.

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The `mptcp_pm_add_timer()` function, executed as a timer callback in softirq context, accesses and modifies socket and MPTCP state without appropriate locking. This leads to a data-race when the same socket is concurrently accessed from process context (e.g., via system calls), potentially corrupting shared data structures. The fix adds `bh_lock_sock()` to synchronize access and reschedules the timer if the socket is already locked by user context.
        
        Commit message:
        mptcp: pm: ADD_ADDR rtx: fix potential data-race

This mptcp_pm_add_timer() helper is executed as a timer callback in
softirq context. To avoid any data races, the socket lock needs to be
held with bh_lock_sock().

If the socket is in use, retry again soon after, similar to what is done
with the keepalive timer.

Fixes: 00cfd77b9063 ("mptcp: retransmit ADD_ADDR when timeout")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Mat Martineau <martineau@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260505-net-mptcp-pm-fixes-7-1-rc3-v1-3-fca8091060a4@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/net/mptcp/pm.c b/net/mptcp/pm.c
index 5056eb8db24e..3912128d9b86 100644
--- a/net/mptcp/pm.c
+++ b/net/mptcp/pm.c
@@ -337,6 +337,13 @@ static void mptcp_pm_add_timer(struct timer_list *timer)
 	if (inet_sk_state_load(sk) == TCP_CLOSE)
 		return;
 
+	bh_lock_sock(sk);
+	if (sock_owned_by_user(sk)) {
+		/* Try again later. */
+		sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + HZ / 20);
+		goto out;
+	}
+
 	if (mptcp_pm_should_add_signal_addr(msk)) {
 		sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + TCP_RTO_MAX / 8);
 		goto out;
@@ -365,6 +372,7 @@ static void mptcp_pm_add_timer(struct timer_list *timer)
 		mptcp_pm_subflow_established(msk);
 
 out:
+	bh_unlock_sock(sk);
 	__sock_put(sk);
 }
